en_alt: Scientists supposed that the Earth was flat.
note: «Учёные» is as often "scientists" as "scholars"; accept both in the drill.

ru: Без фа́ктов я бы не полага́ла так уве́ренно.

note: Compound future of a stative verb: "will be supposing" is not English, so the flat "will suppose" is correct here.

ru: Е́сли бы мог, я полете́л бы в Япо́нию.
en_alt: If I could, I would fly to Japan.
note: The Russian puts the condition first; that order is equally valid English.

en_alt: The plane flew above the clouds.
note: "flew off above the clouds" is strained English, so the plain reading should also be accepted.

ru: В жару́ она́ бу́дет полива́ть огоро́д ка́ждый ве́чер.

en_alt: She put the child in the cot.
note: «ребёнка» is glossed "child" corpus-wide; that rendering should count too.

ru: Я положи́ла бы кни́гу на ме́сто.
en: I would have put the book back in its place.
note: Perfective бы+past is a counterfactual about one completed act, so "would have put"; this also clears the "would put" frame collision with класть.

ru: Ско́ро она́ поло́жит ве́щи в чемода́н.

note: Frame collision with класть is harmless: the imperative distinguishes this sentence from the partner's declarative.

ru: Тепе́рь вы бу́дете получа́ть зарпла́ту два ра́за в ме́сяц.
en: From now on you will be receiving your salary twice a month.
note: "you will be paid" drops зарплату and switches to a passive the Russian does not use; the imperfective compound future is "will be receiving".

ru: Без рабо́ты я бы не получа́ла дохо́да.
note: Imperfective бы+past is rightly a general "would not receive"; the colliding перфектив partner (получить) is the side being fixed.

ru: Мы получа́ем зарпла́ту в конце́ ме́сяца.
Он получа́л хоро́шие отме́тки в шко́ле.
У меня́ не получа́ется реши́ть зада́чу.
Без пра́ктики ничего́ бы не получа́лось.
note: Imperfective habitual "would turn out" is correct here; the perfective partner получиться is the side being fixed.

ru: С но́вым реце́птом пиро́г бу́дет получа́ться вкусне́е.
note: "will be turning out tastier" is not English, so the flat compound future has to stand.

ru: Ско́ро ты полу́чишь отве́т на письмо́.
en_alt: Soon you will receive an answer to your letter.
note: «отве́т» is glossed "answer"; accept that alongside "reply".

ru: Я получи́л бы пре́мию за хоро́шую рабо́ту.
en: I would have received a bonus for good work.
note: Perfective бы+past is a single completed event, so "would have received"; leaves получать's "would not receive" as the only present counterfactual.

ru: Ско́ро у тебя́ полу́чится говори́ть свобо́дно.

note: "succeed" is the everyday rendering of «у тебя́ полу́чится» and should not be marked wrong.

ru: С тако́й кома́ндой всё бы получи́лось.
en: With such a team everything would have turned out well.
note: Perfective бы+past reads as a completed outcome; this leaves получаться's "nothing would turn out well" as the only "would turn out".

ru: Я полюби́ла бы э́тот край всем се́рдцем.
note: The English is right, but «край» is glossed "edge" corpus-wide while it means "region/land" here — the headword gloss is the half that looks too narrow.

ru: Ты полю́бишь э́ту му́зыку со вре́менем.

note: "came to love" is clearly distinct from любить's plain "love", so the frame collision leaves a usable cue.
"came to love" is clearly distinct from любить's plain "love", so the frame collision leaves a usable cue.

en_alt: Soon the noise will interfere with our work.
note: "interfere with" is the more literal rendering of помешать + dative and is equally natural.

en: Excuse me, I'm not disturbing you, am I?
note: "am I not disturbing you?" reads as a rhetorical question; the Russian is a polite negative check, which English makes with a tag question.

ru: Я не помеша́ла бы ва́шему разгово́ру.

en: The rain will spoil our walk.
note: "prevent our walk" is translationese — English prevents a person from doing something, not a walk.

ru: Мы ещё до́лго бу́дем по́мнить э́тот день.
en_alt: We will remember this day for a long time to come.
note: «ещё до́лго» is "for a long time to come"; the current English quietly drops ещё.

ru: Без за́писей я бы не по́мнил дета́ли.
Ра́ньше я помога́ла отцу́ в гараже́.

note: Frame collision with помочь's imperative is answerable — subject and object differ entirely.

ru: Без вас я бы не помога́л так мно́гим.
note: Imperfective бы+past is rightly the general "would not help"; the perfective partner помочь is the side being fixed.
Frame collision with помочь's imperative is answerable — this is a first-person declarative.

en: Soon everyone will be silent for a while as a mark of respect.

Frame collision with помогать is answerable: this is an imperative with a different object.

ru: Ско́ро сосе́д помо́жет нам с ремо́нтом.
Я помогла́ бы тебе́ с перее́здом.
en: I would have helped you with the move.
note: Perfective бы+past is a counterfactual about one completed act; this leaves помогать's "I would not help so many people" as the only present counterfactual.

en_alt: If you need anything, call me.
note: English normally personalises the impersonal понадо́бится; both renderings are valid.

en_alt: Soon warm things will be needed.
note: «ве́щи» is glossed "thing"; accept the literal rendering too.

ru: Без ка́рты нам бы понадо́бился гид.

en_alt: He took the letter to the post office.
note: "took" is the ordinary English for понёс on an errand; accept it alongside the literal "carried off".

ru: Ско́ро река́ понесёт ло́дку к мо́рю.

en: I will carry the bags into the house.
note: "carry off into the house" is self-contradictory — "off" means away; the sibling «Ты понесёшь су́мки в дом?» already drops it.

ru: Со вре́менем ты бу́дешь понима́ть бо́льше.
en: In time you will understand more and more.
note: The imperfective compound future is flattened to a bare "will understand", colliding with three понять sentences; "will be understanding" is not English, so the gradual "more and more" carries the aspect.

ru: Понима́я его́ страх, она́ обняла́ его́.
Без словаря́ я бы не понима́ла текст.
note: Imperfective бы+past is rightly the general "would not understand"; the perfective partner понять is the side being fixed.

en_alt: I did not understand physics before.
note: "before" is the more idiomatic rendering of «ра́ньше» here; accept both.

ru: Без трениро́вки мяч бы ре́дко попада́л в цель.
Без зо́нтика я бу́ду попада́ть под дождь.

note: Frame collision with попасть is answerable — a habitual yes/no question against a "how do we…" question.

ru: Без внима́ния я бы ча́сто попада́лся на оши́бках.
